paragraphs.text: Northwind is hiring its first AI Solutions Engineer to take manual work off its operations, finance and support teams. Most of my best work started as a conversation with someone in operations, not a ticket, so a role that begins with those conversations is the one I want.

At Acme Logistics, support tickets arrived faster than anyone could decide who should answer them. The slow part wasn't the answer; it was the sorting. So I built a Claude-based triage service that reads each ticket and routes it to the right team, about 1,200 a week now, and first responses got 40% faster. That kind of quiet bottleneck is usually where automation pays off first.

Finance had a similar story. Invoice data was typed in by hand, so I automated the entry with document extraction and kept a human review queue in the loop. It saved 30 hours a week, and nobody had to trust a black box to get there. That balance between automation and a person checking the edge cases is how I'd approach your finance work as well.
I'd like to hear which of your teams is carrying the most manual work right now, and talk through where I'd start.
